title: Hes change in a way not to be always and ever wearing the same old hat unless I paid some nicelooking boy to do it since I cant do it myself
html_source: Molly realizes that Bloom probably knows about Boylan’s designs and grants her tacit permission by indicating his plans to be out late. Then ‘…hes change [?] in a way not to be always and ever wearing the same old hat unless I paid some nicelooking boy to do it since I cant do it myself’. The latter part of this passage veers into fantasy about seducing a young boy, but what’s happening in the first part of the passage (hes change…‘), and what can’t Molly do for herself?
